item.title: As Longtime Del. Norton Retires, the Fight for D.C.’s Scattered Continues
item.description: Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.) has been a champion of D.C. statehood and advocate of D.C. residents, but there is still much work to be done to ensure that incarcerated D.C. residents are placed in federal facilities in close proximity to the District, as evidenced by the death of David Blakeney, who died in a Pennsylvania prison due to neglect. The post As Longtime Del. Norton Retires, the Fight for D.C.’s Scattered Continues appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: With New Upgrade, Leckie Education Campus Moves Into the Future
item.description: Leckie Education Campus has completed a two-story addition, providing students with new classrooms, science lab, dining room, and other amenities, as well as improved accessibility and security, and was designed with input from students, faculty, and staff. The post With New Upgrade, Leckie Education Campus Moves Into the Future appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Lifelong Stress and Inflammation Tied to Earlier Deaths Among Black Americans
item.description: A new study has found that Black Americans have higher mortality rates than their white counterparts due to cumulative stress and inflammation, which accounted for nearly half of the observed racial gap in mortality. The post Lifelong Stress and Inflammation Tied to Earlier Deaths Among Black Americans appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: New D.C. Proposal Sends Every Child Support Dollar to Families, Not Government
item.description: The Child Support Improvement Amendment Act of 2026 would ensure that all child support payments go directly to the families in need, rather than being diverted to cover government costs. The post New D.C. Proposal Sends Every Child Support Dollar to Families, Not Government appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Ingrid S. Watson Takes on New Role in Prince George’s County
item.description: Ingrid S. Watson, former District 4 Councilmember, has been appointed as the new president and CEO of Prince George's County's Economic Development Corporation, bringing with her decades of public service experience and a commitment to promoting business development and economic opportunity. The post Ingrid S. Watson Takes on New Role in Prince George’s County appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Where Hoops Meet History: Washington Wizards, Capital City Go-Go Launch Black History Month Activations
item.description: The Washington Wizards and Capital City Go-Go are celebrating Black History Month with a series of activations honoring pioneers of the culture, including themed game nights, giveaways, and a culminating celebration of HBCUs and the Divine Nine. The post Where Hoops Meet History: Washington Wizards, Capital City Go-Go Launch Black History Month Activations appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: CHAVIS: Stop Corporate Consolidation Silencing Local Media Voices
item.description: The National Newspaper Publishers Association (NNPA) and other local news media organizations are urging the FCC to reject the proposed Nexstar-TEGNA merger, which would give Nexstar control over 265 local TV stations and threaten the diversity of viewpoints, independence of local newsrooms, and public's access to locally grounded information. The post CHAVIS: Stop Corporate Consolidation Silencing Local Media Voices appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: In Direct Assault on Free Speech, Journalists Georgia Fort and Don Lemon Arrested by Trump DOJ
item.description: Two Black journalists, Georgia Fort and Don Lemon, were arrested for documenting protests critical of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, which many are calling an attack on the First Amendment. The post In Direct Assault on Free Speech, Journalists Georgia Fort and Don Lemon Arrested by Trump DOJ appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Shutdown Deal Keeps ICE Funded as Democrats Fail to Secure Health Care Protections
item.description: Senate Democrats are moving towards a deal with President Trump to avert a full government shutdown, while preserving full funding for ICE and leaving millions of Americans without protection from rising health care costs. The post Shutdown Deal Keeps ICE Funded as Democrats Fail to Secure Health Care Protections appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Groups Urge House to Block Bill Letting President Pick D.C. Attorney General
item.description: A coalition of 19 nonpartisan nonprofit organizations has urged House leaders to oppose legislation that would end the District of Columbia's elected attorney general and replace it with a presidential appointment, citing concerns that it would damage prosecutorial independence and take power away from the people of the District. The post Groups Urge House to Block Bill Letting President Pick D.C. Attorney General appeared first on The Washington Informer.
